newsitem.title: UK: Emerging market debt dips further, awaits direction.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt dips further, awaits direction.

text.p: Emerging market debt continued soft yet subdued on Friday with selling seen in Asia, dealers said.
But they said players in London were looking to buy in to the market at the lower levels in the hopes that any uncertainties would be shrugged off.
There was also selling of the long global bonds amid continued scares on Brazil and speculation against the real, dealers said.
"We're all waiting for New York to get in to see what direction the market will take," a dealer said. "Some people have fears of a devaluation of Brazil's currency," he added.
Others said the "safest bets" at present were Mexico and Russia, although there was some selling pressure.
"If prices come down players will be looking to buy into weakness," a dealer said.
In New York emerging market debt turned lower prompted by steep losses in the Sao Paolo stock market and a late-day slump in U.S. Treasuries.
At 1200 GMT in London selling outweighed the buyers, Brazil "C" bonds had slipped even further on Friday to trade at 81.0 bid versus levels around 82.625 overnight in New York.
Argentina FRBs were also off at 93.75 versus an overnight 94.0 and Mexico pars at 79.5 versus previous levels around 80.0.
Meanwhile Argentina's planned $750 million seven-year global bond has been put on hold until market conditions allow, bankers said on Friday.
